Guidance & outlook: The company recorded consolidated total revenues of INR794.4 crores in quarter 1 FY27 compared to INR1,390.6 crores in the corresponding quarter last year.

Consolidated profit after tax stood at INR206.5 crores compared to INR269 crores in quarter 4 of FY26, which included onetime benefit of INR115 crores arising from remeasurement of deferred tax assets on MAT credit and other deferred tax assets and liabilities following the company's decision to move to the new tax regime from FY27.
I think this year, we expect that domestic will increase by about 25% in volumes alone.
Growth & demand: The decline is largely attributable to lower Lenalidomide revenue during the quarter, which was partially offset by double -digit growth in the base business.
On a normalized basis, excluding this onetime tax benefit in quarter 4 last year, consolidated PAT grew by 34% quarter-on-quarter.
Revenue from Brazil stood at INR178 crores, representing a growth of 180%.
Margins & costs: EBITDA, including other income for the quarter, stood at INR245.7 crores with EBITDA margin of 30.9%.

There has been an NATCO Pharma Limited August 14, 2026 improvement in EBITDA margin quarter-on-quarter, which can be attributed to the performance of our international and domestic business and lower and measured operating costs.
But typically, I think when we give our guidance, we assume these costs and then we build in the PAT numbers once based on what we believe spend.
Capex & expansion: In July 2026, we acquired additional stake of 13.25% in Adcock Ingram, taking our total holding to 49%.
Sir, so you highlighted that you require cash for your internal capex and some capacity expansion that could be planned.
Organically, I think every year, we have around INR250 crores to INR300 crores of capex year- on-year.
Balance sheet & cash: So you're right, our net cash as of today is around INR1,400 crores.
So we plan according to the cash flow that we have.
Currently, we have around INR1,400 crores of net cash.
Risks & challenges: Also, if we were to just look on a quarter-on-quarter basis, in constant currency terms, there seems to be a 14% kind of decline.
As probably most of you are aware, there has been the El Nino fear and delay in rains.
So that is what actually caused a little bit of delay in the cropping season.
